investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists anywhere in the 6-node cluster. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. Supported by the identical scheduler message across all three sibling checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a node restart, resource leak, or quota reduction), the entire feature becomes unschedulable. The affinity constraint itself may be correct but leaves no scheduling headroom.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota reduction or infrastructure scaling event: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes may have been reduced (e.g., by a node configuration change, VM provider quota limit, or node pool resize) without a corresponding increase in node count or VM slots.

Lower probability — eval runner token or org resolution failure causing a silent early exit: the runner checks for args.token at line 1882 and would skip rather than fail with a scheduler message, so this is ruled out as the primary cause; the scheduler message is explicit infrastructure evidence.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream

This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.

investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness was unable to reach the upstream model provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-08-12T15:37:48Z). The provider field and resolvedModel field in the result for aura-gpt-5-5 are both null, confirming the provider was never resolved. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a transient or sustained upstream provider connectivity issue scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route; no evidence of a user-traffic incident or broader service outage is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists anywhere in the 6-node cluster. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 136s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141230, status=fail, endedAt=2026-08-12T15:40:37.640Z — the check ran well past the 136s unscheduled window and failed before the 360000ms outage threshold.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, matching the empty evidence object.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck 144s, latencyMs=149598 — confirms the capacity problem persisted across a second independent pod request.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=147833 — a third independent pod request also failed to schedule, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod never schedules, no VM ID or state is returned and evidence is never written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. Supported by the identical scheduler message across all three sibling checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a node restart, resource leak, or quota reduction), the entire feature becomes unschedulable. The affinity constraint itself may be correct but leaves no scheduling headroom.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota reduction or infrastructure scaling event: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes may have been reduced (e.g., by a node configuration change, VM provider quota limit, or node pool resize) without a corresponding increase in node count or VM slots.

Lower probability — eval runner token or org resolution failure causing a silent early exit: the runner checks for args.token at line 1882 and would skip rather than fail with a scheduler message, so this is ruled out as the primary cause; the scheduler message is explicit infrastructure evidence.
